newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-LATE TRIES SEAL TENSE LIONS WIN.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-LATE TRIES SEAL TENSE LIONS WIN.

text.p: Two tries in the final eight minutes sealed a momentous victory for the British Lions in the first match of their three-test series against South Africa at Newlands on Saturday.

The Lions had been trailing 16-15 and searching desperately for a flash of match-winning inspiration when scrum-half Matt Dawson sprinted away down the blindside on the Springboks' 22 metre line, selling an outrageous dummy on the way, to put his side ahead
Neil Jenkins, who had kept his side in the match with five out of seven successful penalties, missed the conversion from the right-hand touchline to leave the game in the balance.

But as the Springboks tried to run the ball from their own half, the Lions stole possession and right wing Alan Tait scored in the corner after number eight Tim Rodber had looped a pass over the heads of two defenders.
The win ended a run of seven successive victories for the Springboks and will give the Lions a massive confidence boost in the final two weeks of their first tour of South Africa in 17 years.
But it was the home side who appeared to have the game in their grasp when they entered the final quarter having scored two tries to nil.
Centre Edrich Lubbe kicked them into a 3-0 lead after as many minutes and although Neil Jenkins cancelled it out after six minutes the Springboks kept the pressure on to score the first try.
Prop Os du Randt gathered a tap down from a five metre lineout to bullock over but two further penalties from Jenkins gave the Lions a 9-8 interval lead.
They extended that with a fourth Jenkins penalty immediately after the restart but South Africa's second try once again turned the tide in the home side's favour.
Number eight Gary Teichmann brushed off the tackle of Scott Gibbs down the blindside of a ruck to feed replacement back Russell Bennett who raced over in the left hand corner.
The conversion was missed by fly-half Henry Honiball -- deputising as kicker for the injured Lubbe -- but a penalty in front of the posts for offside at a ruck extended the Springboks lead to 16-12.

The writing appeared to be on the wall for the Lions but Bennett had a potential second try ruled out for a forward pass and a fifth Jenkins penalty took the visiting side into the last 10 minutes trailing by a single point.

The Lions had hardly had any possession in the South African 22 but Dawson, drafted in when Welshman Rob Howley was forced out of the tour by a shoulder injury, made up for it as he scooted away from the tackles of Teichmann and flanker Ruben Kruger to touch down in the corner.

With time running out the South Africans' desperate attempts to break out set up more possession for the Lions in the oppoisiton 22 and with the home side defence over-stretched in the corner, Tait crossed without a hand being laid on him.
The second and third tests are in Durban and Johannesburg on the next two Saturdays.

South Africa - 15-Andre Joubert, 14-James Small, 13-Japie Mulder, 12-Edrich Lubbe (16-Russell Bennett, 40 mins), 11-Andre Snyman, 10-Henry Honiball, 9-Joost van der Westhuizen, 8-Gary Teichmann (captain), 7-Andre Venter, 6-Ruben Kruger, 5-Hannes Strydom 4-Mark Andrews, 3-Adrian Garvey, 2-Naka Drotske, 1-Os du Randt.

British Lions - 15-Neil Jenkins, 14-Ieuan Evans, 13-Jeremy Guscott, 12-Scott Gibbs, 11-Alan Tait, 10-Gregor Townsend, 9-Matt Dawson, 8-Tim Rodber, 7-Richard Hill, 6-Lawrence Dallaglio, 5-Jeremy Davidson, 4-Martin Johnson (captain), 3-Paul Wallace, 2-Keith Wood, 1-Tom Smith (Jason Leonard, 80).
